research_question: When should a multilingual machine-translation workflow route output to human review or expose decision feedback, and when are apparent gains artifacts of language, use case, presentation, or rater disagreement?
decision_owner: Public-service translation owners and interface designers deciding release, review, and feedback policy.
worlds: W1: A calibrated threshold or feedback representation improves fit-for-purpose human decisions.
W2: Apparent gains are specific to language, use case, presentation, synthetic errors, or rater disagreement.
W3: Explicit advice increases trust or over-reliance, while implicit feedback better preserves user agency.
discriminator: A preregistered decision study across at least two use cases and language pairs, with fixed MT outputs, a human-review reference, natural-versus-synthetic error controls, and presentation controls.
falsifier: No decision improvement remains after controls, a single threshold fails to transport, or findings under synthetic errors do not reproduce on naturally occurring errors.
scope: R0 problem framing around fit-for-purpose decisions, not a proposed universal metric or routing method.
does_not_establish: No gap, novelty, prevalence, universal threshold, or lifecycle promotion is established.

source_spans.title: European Commission use of eTranslation
source_spans.locator: eTranslation section, lines 368-375; machine-translation liability section, lines 278-282
source_spans.observation: A live public workflow exposes fully automatic MT with explicit variation by text and language pair and fit-for-purpose exclusions.
source_spans.resolves: Establishes an operational decision context and actor.
source_spans.leaves_unresolved: Which routing or feedback policy improves decisions and at what cost.

source_spans.title: Quality Gate: Estimating the Quality of Machine Translation for Public Administration Use Cases
source_spans.observation: A quality gate formalizes routing but trade-offs vary by language and use case and include rater disagreement.
source_spans.leaves_unresolved: Whether thresholds transport and how human disagreement changes the decision target.

source_spans.title: Supporting User Reliance on Machine Translation via Implicit and Explicit Feedback
source_spans.observation: Feedback form affects reliance and decision accuracy, under narrow conditions.
source_spans.resolves: Supplies a human-decision and agency formulation.
source_spans.leaves_unresolved: Whether effects transport across languages, domains, systems, and natural errors.

derived_questions.question: Does a routing threshold transport across language pairs and assimilation versus dissemination use cases?
derived_questions.smallest_discriminator: A fixed-output comparison with separately calibrated and shared thresholds across two language-use-case cells.

derived_questions.question: Does implicit feedback improve appropriate reliance on naturally occurring critical errors without reducing user agency?
derived_questions.smallest_discriminator: A presentation-controlled decision task contrasting natural and synthetic errors.

controller_boundary: Review-only problem case; independent review is required before route or promotion.
